channel.title: Murmurwkk
channel.description: Murmurwkk writes about AI systems: CUDA operators, distributed training, model deployment and navigation.

item.title: ParScale: Scaling a Language Model with Parallel Streams
item.description: This note explains how ParScale scales a model with parallel streams and refits its scaling law to the released data. With it, a reader can estimate what P streams are worth in parameters and what they cost.

item.title: Testing Sparse Autoencoders on Synthetic Data with Known Features
item.description: I hid 12 known patterns in synthetic data and asked a sparse autoencoder to find them. With 4 active parts per input instead of 2, its error fell threefold, but it found only half of the patterns.

item.title: What TVM Relax Fusion Removes from a Small Program
item.description: Two matmuls became one and five functions became two, yet three temporary matrices survived. This post follows one Relax program down to TIR loops to see what TVM's fusion actually removed.

item.title: CUDA Graphs in an Inference Runtime: What Capture Saves and Binds
item.description: A graph cut a four-kernel attention chain from 33 μs to 12 μs on the GPU, yet the largest full request with copies became slower. This post explains what capture saves, what it binds and when replay is worth it.

item.title: Replacing Gaussian Noise with Student-t in Robust WiFi Positioning
item.description: If a Student-t with 4 degrees of freedom receives the Q of a Gaussian, its covariance doubles. Scale, central pull and tail all change at once; this post separates which change moved a robust WiFi solution, including the failures.

item.title: Three Ways to Densify a WiFi Fingerprint Map and Their Pitfalls
item.description: A WiFi map grew from 1,022 to 4,852 synthetic points yet matched fewer queries after a fix stopped them claiming all 1,045 APs. This post explains three ways to densify a map and their pitfalls.

item.title: Why an XOR Swizzle Slowed a Double-Buffered CUDA GEMM
item.description: An XOR swizzle cut the extra shared wavefronts of a 1024³ FP32 GEMM to zero and its bank conflicts from 6.3 million to 7,399, yet the kernel became 19.5% slower. This post shows where the time went.

item.title: Closing the Gap Between a Naive CUDA GEMM and cuBLAS
item.description: With one output per thread, a 1024³ GEMM took 3.26 ms, while cuBLAS took 0.62 ms. This post covers block tiling, register outer products and float4 loads, checks them in SASS and measures them on square, skinny and short-K shapes.

item.title: INT8 KV-Cache Attention: Thread Mapping and Encoding Error
item.description: Two INT8 decode-attention kernels read the same cache with different thread mappings; one needs a tenth of the QK sectors. A CPU study shows how absmax, rotation and QJL change the output.

item.title: Online Softmax Attention in CUDA and Why It Ran Slower
item.description: Skipping the 16 MiB score matrix of 2048-token attention should save time, yet the online kernel ran slower. This post derives the online state, builds the CUDA kernel, fixes its bugs and shows why the cost lies outside the formula.

item.title: Integrating a Custom SwiGLU CUDA Operator into PyTorch
item.description: The SwiGLU kernel is one sigmoid and two multiplications. To make the operator usable, it must also handle offset views, the current stream, autograd and FakeTensor, and each of these can break it on its own.

item.title: Serial and Parallel Selective-Scan Kernels Compared on a Laptop GPU
item.description: A time-serial scan was fastest in 11 of 12 shapes after its initialization was synchronized, and tied in the twelfth. This post compares six CUDA implementations, tests their allocation cost and varies the number of chains.

item.title: Building TensorRT Engines for One Linear Layer in FP32 and FP16
item.description: One MatMul → Add → Relu graph was built six ways in FP32 and FP16. This post checks which shapes each engine accepts, where FP16 overflows and what a reused execution context really costs per call.

item.title: When to Retire a Navigation Correction and How to Roll It Back
item.description: One translation fixed the early trajectory but damaged the late one. This post discusses how long a navigation correction should stay active, how to detect that it is outdated, and why undoing it requires a fallback that keeps updating.

item.title: Hierarchical AllReduce and the Network-Card Bottleneck
item.description: This note follows one gradient through a hierarchical allreduce and then its bytes to the network card of the node. With it, a reader can check papers such as BlueConnect, TACCL and Trivance against the real bottleneck.

item.title: How Ignoring Cross-Covariance Corrupts a Navigation Velocity Estimate
item.description: With the same observations, the full common source gives a standing person a speed of 0.18 m/s, while independent motion edges give 7 m/s. This post explains the mechanism, the ablation and the diagnostics.

item.title: TF32 on Tensor Cores: Precision Loss and Speed Gain
item.description: TF32 keeps the range of FP32 but sends only 11 bits into the multiplication. This post checks a dot product by hand, the RNA rounding rule and two FP64 references, and measures whether two WMMA kernels are faster.

item.title: Supervising LLM Reasoning: From Chain of Thought to SCoRe
item.description: This note follows CoT, sampling with selection, process rewards, STaR, outcome-reward RL and SCoRe through one worked example. With it, a reader can tell what each method supervises and what it cannot see.

item.title: Scaling Laws: How the Compute-Optimal Training Recipe Changes
item.description: This note explains how the compute-optimal training recipe follows from scaling laws, and how finite data, coupled terms, serving cost and inference compute change it. With it, a reader can redo the choice for a new budget.

item.title: Megatron Tensor Parallelism and FSDP, Derived from a Two-Layer MLP
item.description: This note derives Megatron tensor parallelism, ZeRO and FSDP, and pipeline parallelism from one two-layer MLP. With it, a reader can tell what each method saves and where its communication comes from.

item.title: Attention Sinks and Output Gates: How a Head Outputs Nothing
item.description: This note explains why a softmax head cannot scale its own output, and how attention sinks and output gates let it output almost nothing. With it, a reader can tell when the two mechanisms are equivalent.

item.title: DistServe: Serving Prefill and Decode on Separate GPUs
item.description: This note explains how DistServe serves prefill and decode on separate GPU pools, from goodput and pool sizing to KV transfer. With it, a reader can judge when splitting the two phases pays off.

item.title: Evaluating Navigation Corrections on Held-Out Data with Shared Errors
item.description: Holding out later observations is the right idea, but in navigation all segments share the same inertial, map and device errors. This post shows how to freeze a candidate correction and still score it correctly.

item.title: Using a Phone Barometer for Continuous Height in Indoor Navigation
item.description: All 848 reference points had the right floor, while the height of one route wandered over 20 m. This post shows how a phone's barometer became a continuous height measurement, including the detours and the fixes that had costs.

item.title: Why a First-Order SE(2) Correction Stretches a Trajectory
item.description: A correction reduced the reference error from 24.5 m to 4.8 m but made the route 40% longer. This post shows why a large first-order rotation also scales, checks it on all 146 trajectory edges and fixes it by relinearizing.

item.title: Why Magnetometer Calibration Cannot Determine Heading by Itself
item.description: Ellipsoid calibration fixes the length of each reading, so any rotation of a valid calibration fits equally well. This post explains this rotation freedom, shows when planar motion removes heading information and describes a real column-order bug in the logs.

item.title: Marginalization in a Sliding Window: What It Keeps and What It Costs
item.description: Marginalization keeps old constraints after old states are dropped, including wrong ones. This post derives Schur and QR from a hand-solvable example, replays 700 propagations and measures what a sliding window costs.

item.title: Sharing One WiFi Observation Between Two Navigation Estimators
item.description: When the heading estimator chose WiFi fixes first, the position filter accepted 7 fixes instead of 42, and the heading estimator never produced a correction. Shared evidence needs ownership rules, not just an order.
